title: Conducting spinal cord injury model with clip compression in rodents: Pearls and pitfalls
author: Vahabi, Öztürk

steps.title: Gather instruments and supplies
steps.instruction: Collect all required tools: scalpel with No. 11 blade, micro‑curette, automatic blunt skin retractor (4 in), micro‑Adson forceps, straight‑ended and curved‑ended micro‑rongeurs, Adson forceps, Woodson elevator, micro‑scissors, regular scissors, an aneurysm clip of choice, autoclaved gauzes and cotton‑swabs (use cotton‑swabs for intra‑operative bleeding).

steps.title: Set up magnification
steps.instruction: Wear 5× surgical loupes (preferred over a 10× microscope for practicality and sufficient visibility).

steps.title: Prepare animal and anesthesia
steps.instruction: Select male or female Sprague‑Dawley rats, 8–12 weeks old, weighing 240–420 g. Provide analgesia (paracetamol, tramadol, or ketoprofen). Induce anesthesia with ketamine‑xylazine (40–90 mg/kg ketamine + 5–10 mg/kg xylazine) to obtain 45–90 min of surgical depth; alternatively use inhaled isoflurane for less‑experienced operators.

steps.title: Identify injury level and make skin incision
steps.instruction: Place the rat prone on the surgical table, locate the prominence of T13, and mark a line extending cranially ~3 cm; the midpoint corresponds to the T8–T10 vertebral level where compression will be applied. Make a midline skin incision along this line.

steps.title: Detach paraspinal muscles
steps.instruction: Using a No. 11 blade, make sharp cuts on both sides of the spinous processes, then bluntly separate the muscles with a micro‑curette for three vertebral levels. After adequate exposure, insert a blunt skin retractor at this layer.

steps.title: Perform laminectomy and expose cord
steps.instruction: Confirm the correct vertebral level, then grasp the column cranially to increase inter‑vertebral spacing. Remove the spinous process at the target level with a straight‑ or curved‑ended micro‑rongeur, create a cleavage with the curved rongeur, and continue laminectomy while preserving the dura. Remove sufficient lateral posterior elements so the aneurysm clip can be placed without obstruction.

steps.title: Handle lateral vascular structures
steps.instruction: Avoid damaging the vessels running laterally; if bleeding occurs, compress with autoclaved cotton‑swabs. Excessive bleeding must be controlled promptly to prevent intra‑operative mortality.

steps.title: Place aneurysm clip and time compression
steps.instruction: Select a clip (30 g or 50 g pressure; straight or curved) and position it medio‑laterally so it encircles the entire cord. Start a chronometer and maintain compression for the chosen duration (30 s or 60 s). Adjust clip placement if lateral exposure is insufficient before timing.

steps.title: Evaluate clip function and remove safely
steps.instruction: Confirm clip efficacy by observing cessation of dorsal arterial flow, presence of ecchymosis after removal, and immediate paraplegia with loss of bladder control. Replace the clip after ~50 uses. When removing, fully open the clip before retraction to avoid dura injury.

steps.title: Monitor for hypovolemic shock intra‑operatively
steps.instruction: Watch for significant bleeding; if it occurs, provide sub‑cutaneous serum injections and control hemorrhage with cotton‑swabs to reduce early postoperative mortality.

steps.title: Post‑operative animal monitoring
steps.instruction: House each rat in an individual cage. Observe oral intake, prevent self‑injury (e.g., biting extremities), and apply daily povidone‑iodine to wounds if needed. Monitor for signs of hypovolemia or distress.

steps.title: Collect tissue samples
steps.instruction: After the index surgery, extend the laminectomy proximally and distally (total 1–2 cm of cord) to obtain adequate tissue. Use a Woodson elevator to pass under the cord anteriorly, then make sharp cuts with scissors at both ends to retrieve a clean‑edged sample.

steps.title: Schedule blood collection at euthanasia
steps.instruction: Because tail‑vein sampling is difficult after paraplegia, plan to draw blood at the time of euthanasia rather than during the postoperative period.

steps.title: Provide postoperative care
steps.instruction: Manage the wound, provide soft bedding, and perform bladder massage at least twice daily during the first few days. Continue daily monitoring of bladder function and wound condition; administer antibiotics and increase massage frequency if hematuria or pyuria occurs.
